question: Where was the 12,000-year-old T-shaped pillar featuring a carved human face discovered?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karahantepe.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Archaeologists in southeastern Türkiye have uncovered a 12,000-year-old T-shaped pillar featuring a carved human face at the Karahantepe archaeological site.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The pillar is the first known example of a human face carved on a T-shaped pillar, adding crucial insight into Neolithic symbolism and self-representation.**
 
• **The discovery, announced in October 2025, is part of the ongoing Taş Tepeler (Stone Hills) Project, which explores the emergence of settled life and spiritual practices.**
 
• **The pillar was found in the Şanlıurfa Province, southeastern Türkiye, and dates back to the Pre-Pottery Neolithic period, approximately 12,000 years ago.**
 
• **The T-shaped limestone monolith previously only had arm and hand carvings, making this human face a unique and groundbreaking find.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Taş Tepeler (Stone Hills) Project__

 __
 
• An excavation project investigating Neolithic sites, including Göbekli Tepe, aimed at understanding the origins of settled life and spiritual practices.
 
 
 
• Göbekli Tepe__
 __
 
• One of the most significant archaeological sites, known for its monumental stone structures and carvings, often referred to as the "world’s oldest temple."
 
 
 
• Pre-Pottery Neolithic Period__
 
 
• A period before the widespread use of pottery, marked by the development of early farming and permanent settlements.
